newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: ARGENTINE BONDS END DOWN, TURN ON U.S. TREASURIES.
newsitem.headline: ARGENTINE BONDS END DOWN, TURN ON U.S. TREASURIES.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished lower Friday, pulled down by a technical decline in U.S. Treasuries, with some traders predicting a larger correction.
"There had not been a sufficiently big correction," said a trader at a foreign bank, pointing to the declines at the end of last week. "Today was pretty surprising."
The market started off on a strong note, boosted by general strength in emerging debt markets on the back of signs that Russia is nearing a deal to restructure its commercial debt.
But prices turned as U.S. Treasuries fell in the afternoon.
Argentina's Par Brady bond was down 3/8 at 74-1/2, while the FRB bond fell 1/8 to 95-1/2.

As the Argentine market remains highly correlated with U.S. Treasuries it was not able to avoid the negative impact but spreads were slightly lower, something which could lead to more declines in the Argentine market.
"I think there will be a period of caution - everybody is thinking about their strategy for next week," said another trader.
In the money market, the three-month peso BAIBOR, or Buenos Aires interbank offered rate, was flat at 7.1875 percent.
